examples.text: Czyś był na Rodos oglądać miejsce, gdzie stał kolos?
examples.translation: Were you at Rodos to look at the place where the colussus stood?
examples.english: Were you at Rodos to look at the place where the colussus stood?

glosses: colossus (creature or thing of gigantic size)

examples.text: Skoro brytyjskie statki miały dwa lub trzy kominy, nowy niemiecki kolos musiał przyćmić ich sławę.
examples.translation: Since the British ships had two or three stacks, the new German colossus had to steal their thunder.
examples.english: Since the British ships had two or three stacks, the new German colossus had to steal their thunder.

glosses: colossus (very tall or powerfully built person)
midterm exam conducted mainly by a university

A statue of gigantic size. The name was especially applied to certain famous statues in antiquity, as the Colossus of Nero in Rome and the Colossus of Rhodes, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
Any creature or thing of gigantic size.

examples.text: ["]The Empire has always been a realm of colossal resources. […] Why, they don't even understand their own colossi any longer. The machines work from generation to generation automatically, and the caretakers are a hereditary caste who would be helpless if a single D-tube in all that vast structure burnt out.["]
What I love about the colossi is that they actually feel colossal : they move ponderously around, sending out tremours with each step; their ancient husks richly detailed with dirt and plant life.

glosses: Somebody or something very greatly admired and respected.

examples.text: The truth is that [Isaac] Newton was very much a product of his time. The colossus of science was not the first king of reason, [John Maynard] Keynes wrote after reading Newton’s unpublished manuscripts. Instead “he was the last of the magicians”.
Nie pójdę dziś z wami na piwo, bo mam jutro kolosa ze statystyki.
